title: Pentagon UFO files reveal mysterious radar detections suggesting Mach 2.5 flight — but there's a catch
excerpt: The 2023 incident was disclosed Friday as part of a sweeping release of government UFO records.
content:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A newly released Pentagon report details a mysterious series of radar detections suggesting a UFO traveled at a blistering 1,650 mph before changing direction — although investigators couldn’t determine whether the signals came from a single craft.

The 2023 incident, disclosed Friday as part of a sweeping release of government UFO records, involved eight radar detections over 84 seconds at an estimated altitude of 55,000 to 70,000 feet.

A civilian air-surveillance radar system recorded signals that, if they came from the same object, would indicate a minimum average ground speed of approximately Mach 2.5, according to the Pentagon’s All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office.

The analysis calculated a combined distance of 38.5 miles between the eight detections, with successive segments suggesting a 39-degree counterclockwise change in direction after approximately 48 seconds.

Marik von Rennenkampff, a former State and Defense Department official, said the case marked the first time the government’s UFO archive included an analysis of radar tracks.

The findings, however, came with a significant caveat.

Investigators acknowledged that the radar’s 12-second sweep interval was insufficient to establish whether all eight detections originated from the same object or represented a continuous flight path.

The analysis also cautioned that the line connecting the signals showed the shortest distances between successive detections — not the object’s actual trajectory.

The incident was among 43 files released Friday in the Pentagon’s eighth tranche of records documenting unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAPs, the government’s preferred term for UFOs.

The collection included 40 documents and three videos, as well as previously undisclosed details about a Pentagon-funded contractor’s efforts to investigate extraordinary phenomena.

Among the records was a 538-page report from Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, or BAASS, a private contractor that conducted research for the Defense Intelligence Agency.

The July 2009 document outlined plans to build a 5,000-square-foot underground vault with three-foot-thick concrete walls to store potentially recovered hardware and biological samples.

The proposed facility was intended to house what the contractor described as “exotic material or tissue” that it hoped to acquire from private individuals and organizations, including sources in Brazil.

The records do not establish that the vault was ever completed or that the contractor obtained extraterrestrial materials.

BAASS also investigated unusual activity at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property associated with reports of UFO sightings and paranormal phenomena.

The Pentagon-funded research was part of the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program, which received approximately $22 million in government funding.

Another newly released file documents a 1953 UFO sighting reported by Clarence “Kelly” Johnson, the famed Lockheed aircraft designer behind the company’s secret Skunk Works operation.

Johnson described watching a dark, elliptical object near his California ranch that initially appeared motionless before rapidly receding into the distance.

A Lockheed flight-test crew reported seeing an unusual object around the same time.

“I am now more firmly convinced than ever that such devices exist,” Johnson wrote in his report, referring to flying saucers.

The Air Force ultimately classified the sighting as a lenticular cloud — a naturally occurring formation that can resemble a saucer.

Friday’s release also included three previously undisclosed military videos from the Middle East, recorded in 2020, 2023 and 2026.

The infrared and electro-optical footage showed unidentified areas of contrast being tracked by military sensors, although the publicly released clips lacked sufficient information to establish the objects’ size or speed.

The Pentagon has not determined what caused the observations.

The latest disclosure is part of a broader effort by Washington to make UFO records public, with additional releases planned as Trump administration officials continue reviewing documents held by federal agencies.
